events.title: Canada adopts the Maple Leaf Flag
events.summary: A royal proclamation brings in Canada's national flag.
events.description: On February 15, 1965, Canada officially adopted the Maple Leaf Flag following a royal proclamation.
events.notificationTitle: A leaf becomes a nation's flag
events.notificationBody: In 1965, Canada officially adopted the Maple Leaf Flag.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 15

events.title: The USS Maine explodes in Havana Harbor
events.summary: The sinking of the US battleship precedes the Spanish-American War.
events.description: On February 15, 1898, an explosion sank the US battleship Maine while it lay at anchor in Havana Harbor, Cuba.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 15

events.title: The last Soviet troops leave Afghanistan
events.summary: The occupation that began in 1979 comes to an end.
events.description: On February 15, 1989, the Soviet Union withdrew its last troops from Afghanistan, which it had occupied since 1979.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 15

events.title: Susan B. Anthony is born
events.summary: The pioneer of women's suffrage is born in Massachusetts.
events.description: On February 15, 1820, Susan B. Anthony, a pioneer of the women's suffrage movement, was born in Adams, Massachusetts.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 15

events.title: Galileo Galilei is born in Pisa
events.summary: The astronomer who will discover Jupiter's largest moons is born.
events.description: On February 15, 1564, Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa. He later discovered the four largest moons of Jupiter, now called the Galilean moons.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Galileo

events.title: The Kyoto Protocol takes effect
events.summary: The climate treaty enters into force more than seven years after its adoption.
events.description: On February 16, 2005, the Kyoto Protocol, an agreement to reduce emissions of gases that contribute to global warming, went into effect, more than seven years after its adoption in Kyoto, Japan, in December 1997.
events.notificationBody: In 2005, the Kyoto Protocol to cut greenhouse gas emissions came into force.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 16
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Kyoto Protocol

events.title: Lithuania declares independence
events.summary: The 20-member Taryba proclaims an independent state.
events.description: On February 16, 1918, the 20-member Taryba, Lithuania's national council, proclaimed the country an independent state.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 16

events.title: Wallace Carothers patents nylon
events.summary: The DuPont chemist patents the first fully synthetic fiber.
events.description: On February 16, 1937, the DuPont chemist Wallace Hume Carothers patented nylon.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 16

events.title: Fidel Castro becomes premier of Cuba
events.summary: The revolutionary leader takes charge of the government.
events.description: On February 16, 1959, Fidel Castro became premier of Cuba.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 16

events.title: Lincoln meets the girl who suggested his beard
events.summary: On his way to Washington, he stops to see 12-year-old Grace Bedell.
events.description: On February 16, 1861, President-elect Abraham Lincoln stopped at Westfield, New York, and met 12-year-old Grace Bedell, who had written to suggest that he grow a beard.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 16

events.title: Garry Kasparov defeats IBM's Deep Blue
events.summary: The world chess champion wins his first match against the computer.
events.description: On February 17, 1996, world chess champion Garry Kasparov triumphed over IBM's Deep Blue computer.
events.notificationBody: In 1996, world chess champion Garry Kasparov triumphed over IBM's Deep Blue computer.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 17

events.title: Kosovo declares independence from Serbia
events.summary: Not every country recognizes the new republic.
events.description: On February 17, 2008, Kosovo declared its independence from Serbia, though a number of countries refused to recognize the new republic.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 17

events.title: The Hunley becomes the first submarine to sink an enemy ship
events.summary: The Confederate submarine attacks the USS Housatonic off Charleston.
events.description: On February 17, 1864, the Confederate submarine Hunley became the first submarine to sink an enemy ship when it attacked the USS Housatonic off Charleston, South Carolina.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 17

events.title: Puccini's Madama Butterfly premieres at La Scala
events.summary: The opera opens in Milan and becomes one of the most often performed.
events.description: On February 17, 1904, Giacomo Puccini's Madama Butterfly premiered at La Scala in Milan. It became one of the most frequently performed operas.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 17

events.title: The House of Representatives elects Thomas Jefferson president
events.summary: A tie in the electoral college is broken by the House.
events.description: On February 17, 1801, following a tie in the electoral college, the US House of Representatives elected Thomas Jefferson president.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 17

events.title: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto
events.summary: A 24-year-old with no formal training in astronomy finds a new world.
events.description: On February 18, 1930, Clyde Tombaugh, a 24-year-old American with no formal training in astronomy, discovered the dwarf planet Pluto.
events.notificationBody: In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh, 24 and with no formal astronomy training, discovered Pluto.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 18

events.title: Martin Luther dies in Eisleben
events.summary: The leader of the Protestant Reformation dies at 62.
events.description: On February 18, 1546, Martin Luther, leader of the Protestant Reformation, died at age 62 in Eisleben, Saxony.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 18

events.title: Shani Davis wins Olympic gold in speed skating
events.summary: He is the first Black athlete to win an individual Winter Olympics gold medal.
events.description: On February 18, 2006, the American speed skater Shani Davis won the men's 1,000-meter long-track final, becoming the first Black athlete to win an individual Winter Olympics gold medal.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 18

events.title: Yoko Ono is born
events.summary: The Japanese artist and musician is born.
events.description: On February 18, 1933, the artist and musician Yoko Ono was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 18

events.title: Ramakrishna is born in Bengal
events.summary: The Hindu mystic and priest is born.
events.description: On February 18, 1836, the Hindu mystic and priest Ramakrishna was born in Hooghly (now Hugli), Bengal, India.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 18

events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus is born in Torun
events.summary: The astronomer who put the Sun at the center of the planets is born.
events.description: On February 19, 1473, the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus was born in Torun, Poland. He argued that Earth is a planet that orbits the Sun.
events.notificationTitle: The man who moved the Earth
events.notificationBody: In 1473, Nicolaus Copernicus, who argued that Earth orbits the Sun, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 19
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Nicolaus Copernicus

events.title: Thomas Edison patents the phonograph
events.summary: A needle's vibrations are used to record and play back sound.
events.description: On February 19, 1878, the American inventor Thomas Edison patented the phonograph, a device that reproduced sound through a needle's vibration.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 19

events.title: Roosevelt signs Executive Order 9066
events.summary: The order forces Japanese Americans into detention camps.
events.description: On February 19, 1942, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, which forced Japanese Americans into detention camps during World War II.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 19

events.title: Deng Xiaoping dies
events.summary: China's paramount leader dies at 92.
events.description: On February 19, 1997, the Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping died at age 92.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 19

events.title: Fidel Castro resigns as president of Cuba
events.summary: He steps down after 19 months out of public view.
events.description: On February 19, 2008, Fidel Castro, after 19 months out of the public eye, formally resigned as president of Cuba.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 19

events.title: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit Earth
events.summary: He circles the planet three times.
events.description: On February 20, 1962, John H. Glenn, Jr., became the first American to orbit Earth, circling it three times.
events.notificationBody: In 1962, John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth, circling it three times.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 20

events.title: The volcano Paricutin begins erupting in Mexico
events.summary: A new volcano bursts out in Michoacan.
events.description: On February 20, 1943, the volcano Paricutin, in Michoacan state, Mexico, began erupting.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 20

events.title: Marinetti names Futurism in Le Figaro
events.summary: An Italian writer launches an art movement in a Paris newspaper.
events.description: On February 20, 1909, the Italian writer Filippo Tommaso Marinetti coined the term Futurism in the Paris newspaper Le Figaro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 20

events.title: Ansel Adams is born
events.summary: The photographer of the American West is born.
events.description: On February 20, 1902, the American photographer Ansel Adams was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 20

events.title: Ludwig Boltzmann is born
events.summary: The Austrian physicist is born.
events.description: On February 20, 1844, the Austrian physicist Ludwig Boltzmann was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 20

events.title: Richard Nixon becomes the first sitting US president to visit China
events.summary: The visit opens a new chapter in Cold War diplomacy.
events.description: On February 21, 1972, Richard Nixon became the first sitting US president to visit China.
events.notificationBody: In 1972, Richard Nixon became the first sitting US president to visit China.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 21

events.title: The Battle of Verdun begins
events.summary: One of the most devastating battles of World War I opens.
events.description: On February 21, 1916, the Battle of Verdun, one of the most devastating engagements of World War I, began.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 21

events.title: Malcolm X is assassinated
events.summary: The Black leader is killed while giving a speech in Manhattan.
events.description: On February 21, 1965, Malcolm X was assassinated while giving a speech in Manhattan.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 21

events.title: The New Yorker begins publication
events.summary: Harold Ross launches the weekly magazine.
events.description: On February 21, 1925, the American weekly magazine The New Yorker began publication under its editor Harold W. Ross.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 21

events.title: Police fire on Bangla language protesters in Dhaka
events.summary: The killings make February 21 a day to honor mother languages.
events.description: On February 21, 1952, students and activists protested at the University of Dhaka for recognition of their language, Bangla (Bengali). Police opened fire, killing seven people. UNESCO later chose February 21 as International Mother Language Day.

sources.name: University of Cambridge - Celebrating language diversity
UNESCO - International Mother Language Day
